notice: RN bank batch 142: Maternity case studies: third-trimester visit, Rh sensitization, GDM with hypoglycemia and traumatic abruption, with four standalone items. questions.stem: A client on the postpartum unit has a new emergency. Using the note, fill in the bowtie: the most likely condition in the middle, two actions to take now on the left and two parameters to monitor on the right.

actions.text: Put a padded tongue blade between the teeth to protect the tongue
Restrain the arms and legs to prevent injury during the seizure
Give a large IV fluid bolus to protect the kidneys

rationale.correct: A postpartum seizure with severe hypertension is eclampsia; give magnesium and protect the airway.

perOption.c1: A seizure with severe-range blood pressure after birth.
perOption.c3: No seizure history; blood pressure is severe.
perOption.c4: Too late after birth; no collapse.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: For each postpartum breast problem, choose the best nursing advice.

cells.text: Both breasts hard, warm, swollen; baby struggles to latch
Tender lump in one breast, no fever

options.text: Feed often; express a little milk to soften the areola before latching; cold packs after feeds
Stop breastfeeding for 2 days
Start antibiotics
Feed often, starting on that side; gentle massage toward the nipple
Avoid feeding from that side
Wear a tight bra
Wear a supportive bra, apply cold packs and avoid stimulating the breasts
Pump to relieve the fullness
Use warm showers on the breasts

rationale.correct: Engorgement and plugged ducts need frequent emptying; suppression needs no stimulation.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: On an antepartum unit, four clients call at once. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client at 30 weeks with placenta previa who has new bright red bleeding soaking a pad
A client at 28 weeks with hyperemesis who vomited once after breakfast
A client at 34 weeks with gestational diabetes whose glucose is 128 mg/dL after lunch
A client at 32 weeks on bed rest asking for help to the bathroom

rationale.correct: Active bleeding with previa is the priority.

perOption.a: Active hemorrhage threatens mother and fetus.

questions.stem: A client at 6 cm without an epidural has intense constant lower back pain, and the fetus is occiput posterior. The client has not voided for 4 hours. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Apply firm counterpressure to the sacrum
Encourage hands-and-knees or side-lying positions
Help the client empty the bladder or catheterize if unable
Offer a warm pack or shower
Keep the client flat on the back
Tell the client back pain is not part of labor

rationale.correct: Counterpressure, positions, bladder care and warmth.
